solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A cold church with altar, perhaps quiet inside, all right?

indicators.note: inside says the quiet letter is placed within the string built from the other pieces

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
CE is the Church of England
an altar is one example of a table, hence 'perhaps'
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a chilly church with its altar, kept hushed, is in good order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something acceptable is satisfactory, so it is all right; the question mark matches the tentative tone.

clue.text: Old ship shedding first bit of load

indicators.note: shedding first bit of means the load word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a cargo is a ship's load

explanation.surface: An ancient vessel unloads part of its freight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the legendary ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth.

clue.text: Coin left to be put in the middle

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
red stands for the political left

explanation.surface: Instructions for a coin left behind to be placed at the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Something centred has been positioned at the midpoint, the past participle matching 'put'.

clue.text: Things that have got stuck coming through the letter box?

definitions.text: Things that have got stuck coming through the letter box?

parts.words: Things that have got stuck coming through the letter box?
parts.note: suggests jammed items, but means the gummed labels that are fixed onto envelopes delivered by post

explanation.walkthrough: 'Got stuck' sounds like jammed in the flap; the items were stuck on, glued to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Postage stamps are adhesive and are fixed to the envelopes that arrive through a letter box.

clue.text: Fool is last to accept help

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: last to means take the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A fool is the final person to take assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to aid someone, a straight synonym for the verb help.

clue.text: The French game in which one's sealed fate

parts.note: la is French for 'the'

indicators.note: sealed means shut inside, so the letter is enclosed by the game

parts.note: chess is a board game
one's reads as 'one is'; one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A French game where someone's destiny is decided.
explanation.definitionFit: Lachesis is one of the three Fates of Greek myth, who measures the thread of life.

clue.text: Woman associated with Dover always?

indicators.note: the letters are associated with, i.e. contained within, the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A quiz question about which woman is linked with Dover, as Vera Lynn is through 'The White Cliffs of Dover'.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the end of 'Dover' and the start of 'always'; the surface nods to the singer Vera Lynn, famous for 'The White Cliffs of Dover'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a female first name, so it fits a clue asking for a woman.

clue.text: The pap I dished out for an inscription

indicators.note: dished out suggests the letters served up in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone served mushy food for a written dedication.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is the words carved on a tombstone, a kind of inscription.

clue.text: Corrective final word beginning to disturb a politician

parts.note: amen is the final word of a prayer

indicators.note: beginning to means take the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A last word that starts to unsettle a Conservative MP, offered as a correction.
explanation.definitionFit: Amendatory means serving to amend, putting right faults, so it is a synonym of remedial.

clue.text: Book group

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the first book of the Bible
second meaning: the English rock band of Phil Collins and Peter Gabriel

explanation.walkthrough: Two bare words, each a separate meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the opening Old Testament book and to a famous progressive rock band.

clue.text: Tea with insects in holy vessel

parts.note: cha (or char) is informal British slang for tea
lice are small parasitic insects

explanation.surface: An unappetising picture of tea crawling with bugs, served in a sacred cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is the cup that holds wine at the Eucharist, a sacred drinking vessel.

clue.text: A historian out somehow to get official recognition

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters arranged by some unspecified means into a new order

explanation.surface: A scholar out of favour somehow wins formal approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; the thirteen letters need it.
explanation.definitionFit: Authorisation is formal permission or sanction granted by those in charge.

clue.text: Paper covering for king size bed?

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: a king size bed is broad, so its covering would be a broad sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsheet is a full-size quality newspaper, as opposed to a tabloid, so it is a kind of paper.

clue.text: A divine tot

parts.note: a divine is a clergyman or theologian; DD is Doctor of Divinity

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small drink or a child, but here it is the verb 'tot up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up figures is to sum them, a synonym for this verb.

clue.text: Minister to turn up, pursuing opportunity

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so this piece comes after the opportunity word

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to roll is to turn over

explanation.surface: A politician arrives in pursuit of an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is the UK government's finance minister.

clue.text: Hard borders or not?

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
edges are borders

explanation.surface: A question whether some boundaries are firm ones, as in the political debate over a hard border.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: hedges are borders that may or may not be firm, and 'or not?' also hints at hedging, refusing to commit either way.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedges are living field boundaries, soft rather than solid walls, and to hedge is to avoid a firm yes or no.

clue.text: Danger from missile to make one hectic or mad

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters of 'hectic or' going wild and reshuffling

explanation.surface: A warning about a bullet whose rebound makes someone frantic or crazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is not I here: the eight letters come wholly from 'hectic or'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ricochet is a bullet or shot rebounding off a surface, a hazard to bystanders.

clue.text: Most dictatorial, so is best to work with!

indicators.note: to work means the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A domineering person's claim that it is best to collaborate.
explanation.definitionFit: Bossiest is the superlative of bossy, most inclined to order others about.

clue.text: Denial, say, impeding country

indicators.note: impeding means getting in the way, so the short piece sits in the middle of the country

parts.note: a nation is a country
e.g. means 'for example', as 'say' does

explanation.surface: A government's refusal is described as obstructing the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A negation is a contradiction or refusal, the act of saying something is not so.

clue.text: Disreputable men chatter when hiding ill-gotten gains

indicators.note: hiding means the chatter word conceals the gains within it

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
loot is stolen goods

explanation.surface: Crooks gossip while concealing their stolen money.
explanation.definitionFit: Galoots are clumsy, oafish fellows, informal for awkward louts.

clue.text: Surgeon in hospital is terrific

indicators.note: in says the answer lies within the following words, across their boundaries

explanation.surface: Praise for a surgeon who is excellent at work in the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Lister was the British pioneer of antiseptic surgery, a famous surgeon.

clue.text: Bird maybe to wobble, having swallowed worm initially

indicators.note: having swallowed means the wobble word takes the letter inside it

parts.note: to teeter is to wobble unsteadily

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word beside it

explanation.surface: A bird totters after gulping down a worm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' suggests a feathered creature, but the answer is anything that tweets.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeter is something that tweets, and a bird chirping is one such, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: The woman's workplace set up tea

parts.note: her is the possessive for 'the woman's'

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is placed upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a lab, or laboratory, is a scientist's workplace

explanation.surface: She arranges tea at her place of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal is an infusion made from herbs rather than tea leaves, a kind of tea.

clue.text: 'orrible place, more than a yard

indicators.note: the dropped H of 'orrible tells us to drop the H of the place word too, Cockney style

parts.note: hell is the place of the damned

explanation.surface: A Cockney grumble about a horrible spot, oddly measured as over a yard.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old cloth measure of 45 inches, so it exceeds a yard of 36 inches.

clue.text: Awful Eve's bad with him — was naughty

indicators.note: awful suggests a bad mess, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eden gossip: Eve's dreadful behaviour with Adam when they sinned.
explanation.definitionFit: To have misbehaved is to have behaved badly, a straight synonym for being naughty.

clue.text: Row that's loud expected to arise

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: in a down clue, to arise means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: due means expected

explanation.surface: A noisy argument that everyone expected to break out.
explanation.definitionFit: A feud is a bitter, lasting quarrel, and a row is a quarrel.

clue.text: Seek spills at back of small room, making inspection

indicators.note: at back of puts the rearranged letters after the room word

parts.note: the loo, or 'smallest room', is British slang for the toilet

indicators.note: spills suggests the letters tumbling out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone searching behind the toilet finds things spilled there and takes a look.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-see is an informal quick look, a brief survey or examination.

clue.text: Something hairy in English city, very roughly reported

indicators.note: said aloud loosely, the city's name comes close to the answer, hence 'very roughly'

parts.note: Bristol is a city in south-west England

explanation.surface: A news report, rather imprecise, of something shaggy found in an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: A bristle is a short stiff hair, as on a brush or a boar.

clue.text: Impetuous artist shut up

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A hot-headed painter is told to be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means acting hastily without thought, the same as being headlong.

clue.text: What makes a girl stand around in city?

indicators.note: around suggests the letters moved about into another order

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about what would make a girl stand about in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalingrad, now Volgograd, was the Russian city of the famous Second World War siege.
